newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan jobless rate hits annual record, to stay high.
newsitem.headline: Japan jobless rate hits annual record, to stay high.

text.p: Japan's unemployment rate hit a record high last year amid a slow recovery in the economy, and no significant improvement is likely in the near term, the government said Friday.
The unemployment rate for 1996 rose to 3.4 percent from 3.2 percent the previous year, government data showed.
Although still far below the double-digit rates of some industrialised countries, it was the highest level since 1953, the earliest year for which comparative figures are available.
"It is difficult to expect a sharp fall in the unemployment rate," a government official told reporters.
He said the rate was gradually falling on a month-on-month basis, but it was doing so at a snail's pace.

The monthly data for December, also released on Friday, showed that the jobless rate remained unchanged from November at 3.3 percent. It has been moving between 3.3 percent and 3.4 percent after hitting a record high of 3.5 percent in May and June.
Economists said a drastic improvement was unlikely in face of a slow recovery by the economy, the outlook for which is clouded by a planned rise in the consumption tax from April.
The economy has been struggling to recover from the long slump that followed the bursting of the 1980s asset "bubble," with the number of bankruptcies still high.
